incidents.label: London Gatwick Airport
incidents.description: Repeated drone sightings near the runway shut Gatwick for roughly 36 hours, cancelling about 1,000 flights and affecting 140,000 passengers. It was the biggest drone disruption at a European airport before the 2025 wave.

incidents.label: Norwegian offshore oil & gas platforms
incidents.description: Unidentified drones appeared at more than 10 Norwegian offshore oil and gas facilities, including inside the 500 m safety zone at Gina Krog and near Equinor's Johan Sverdrup field.

incidents.label: Frankfurt Airport
incidents.description: Drones halted all traffic at Frankfurt, one of Europe's busiest airports, on two days in 2023. Between 2017 and 2023, drones disrupted operations there on 26 separate dates.

incidents.label: Lithuania drone crossings
incidents.description: Two Gerbera drones crossed from Belarus into Lithuania during the September 2025 wave. One carried an explosive warhead.

incidents.label: Poland airspace incursion
incidents.description: About 23 Russian drones crossed from Belarus into Polish airspace overnight on 9-10 September; Polish F-16s and Dutch F-35s downed several, Poland invoked NATO Article 4 and the incursion triggered Operation Eastern Sentry.

incidents.label: Romania airspace incursion
incidents.description: Two Romanian F-16s tracked a Russian Geran drone through Romanian airspace for nearly an hour on 13 September. Romania was the second NATO state to have its airspace breached during the wave.

incidents.label: Latvia drone wreckage
incidents.description: Remains of a drone similar to those used in the Polish and Lithuanian incursions were recovered on Latvia's Baltic coast in mid-September 2025.

incidents.label: Estonia airspace violation
incidents.description: Three Russian MiG-31 jets entered Estonian airspace near Vaindloo for about twelve minutes without flight plans or transponders; Italian F-35s on Baltic Air Policing intercepted them and Estonia invoked NATO Article 4.

incidents.label: Billund Airport
incidents.description: Denmark's second-busiest airport and the gateway to Legoland closed for several hours after air traffic controllers reported multiple unidentified drones, a day before the larger Copenhagen incident.

incidents.label: Copenhagen Airport
incidents.description: Two to three large drones flown by a 'capable operator' closed Copenhagen Airport for nearly four hours, cancelling more than 100 flights; PM Mette Frederiksen called it the most serious attack on Danish critical infrastructure to date.

incidents.label: Oslo Gardermoen Airport
incidents.description: Oslo's main airport closed for about three hours the same night as Copenhagen after two separate drone sightings. Together the two closures disrupted more than 20,000 passengers.

incidents.label: Aalborg Airport
incidents.description: The combined civil-military airport at Aalborg closed twice within roughly 24 hours after repeated drone sightings, part of one coordinated night of drone activity over several Danish airports.

incidents.label: Esbjerg & Sonderborg Airports
incidents.description: Police reported drone activity near Esbjerg and Sonderborg airports on the same night as the wider Danish wave, which officials characterised as a hybrid operation meant to sow fear.

incidents.label: Skrydstrup Air Base
incidents.description: Drones were reported over Skrydstrup, Denmark's main fighter base and home to its F-16s and incoming F-35s, during the late-September wave over Danish military and civil sites.

incidents.label: Kiel naval & infrastructure sites
incidents.description: Drone formations overflew the ThyssenKrupp Marine Systems naval shipyard, Kiel University Hospital, a power plant and the state parliament; authorities opened an espionage and sabotage investigation.

incidents.label: Karup Air Base
incidents.description: Drones were seen for several hours over Karup, Denmark's largest military base and home to its helicopter wing, and the base's civil airspace closed for a time.

incidents.label: Orland Main Air Station
incidents.description: Drones were reported over about two and a half hours at Orland, the main air station for Norway's F-35 fleet, during the late-September Nordic wave.

incidents.label: Elsenborn military camp
incidents.description: Belgian defence officials reported about 15 drones over the Elsenborn military training area that then flew across the border toward Duren in Germany.

incidents.label: Munich Airport
incidents.description: Munich Airport closed twice in under 24 hours after drone sightings. The first night grounded 17 flights and about 3,000 passengers; the second disrupted roughly 6,500 more.

incidents.label: Berlin Brandenburg Airport
incidents.description: Berlin Brandenburg Airport suspended operations for almost two hours after unidentified drones were detected in nearby airspace.

incidents.label: Kleine Brogel Air Base
incidents.description: Unidentified drones were repeatedly observed over the Kleine Brogel air base, which stores US nuclear weapons. Belgium asked the UK for anti-drone support.

incidents.label: Brussels Airport
incidents.description: Belgium's busiest hub closed twice on 4 November after drone sightings, cancelling 54 flights and stranding hundreds of passengers overnight. Disruption continued for days.

incidents.label: Gothenburg-Landvetter Airport
incidents.description: Drone sightings at Gothenburg-Landvetter, Sweden's second-busiest airport, forced inbound flights to divert, some to Copenhagen.

incidents.label: Liege Airport
incidents.description: One of Europe's largest cargo airports halted flights several times for roughly 30 minutes each as drones were detected nearby in early November.

incidents.label: Doel Nuclear Power Station
incidents.description: Three drones were reported above the Doel nuclear power station during Belgium's November wave of unexplained drone overflights.

incidents.label: Volkel Air Base
incidents.description: Dutch forces opened fire at drones over Volkel air base, a nuclear-weapons storage site, but recovered no wreckage.

incidents.label: Dublin Airport area
incidents.description: Several unidentified drones were spotted north of Dublin and over the Irish Sea as Ukrainian President Zelensky's flight approached. Security services responded.

incidents.label: Ile Longue naval base
incidents.description: Five unidentified drones were spotted over Ile Longue, the operational base for France's nuclear ballistic-missile submarines; soldiers used a jammer but downed none.

incidents.label: Immelmann Air Base
incidents.description: Internal military documents recorded about 23 unidentified drones circling the Bundeswehr's Immelmann air base for several hours. The troops had no way to shoot them down and could only watch.

incidents.label: Varena drone crash
incidents.description: A stray Ukrainian strike drone, pushed off course by Russian electronic warfare, crashed at Lake Lavysas. It was the first incident in the 2026 Baltic series.

incidents.label: Auvere power station
incidents.site: Auvere power station, near the Russian border
incidents.description: A stray Ukrainian drone struck the chimney of the Auvere power station near the Russian border; no operational damage was reported.

incidents.label: Kouvola drone crashes
incidents.description: Two Ukrainian long-range attack drones crashed near Kouvola in southeastern Finland, about 50 km from the Russian border. Finland scrambled F/A-18 fighters to identify them and attributed the diversions to Russian jamming.

incidents.label: Rezekne oil depot strike
incidents.description: Two suspected stray drones entered from Russia; one exploded at an oil storage depot near Rezekne and damaged four empty tanks. Within a week the political fallout had brought down the Latvian government.

incidents.label: NATO F-16 shootdown, Estonia
incidents.description: A Romanian Air Force F-16 on NATO Baltic Air Policing shot down a stray drone over Estonia, the first time an Allied fighter downed an aircraft in Estonian airspace.

incidents.label: Vilnius Airport shutdown
incidents.site: Vilnius Airport and the Vilnius region
incidents.description: Lithuania closed the airspace over Vilnius airport and scrambled NATO Baltic Air Policing jets after a suspected drone crossed from Belarus. Residents were told to shelter, trains stopped, and the president and prime minister were moved to secure locations. The drone was never found.

incidents.label: Munich Airport (2026)
incidents.description: Munich Airport halted flights for about an hour after pilots reported a drone over the field; 33 flights were cancelled and more than 20 diverted. Police sweeps found nothing.

incidents.label: NATO Rafale shootdown, Latvia
incidents.description: French Rafales on NATO Baltic Air Policing shot down a stray drone over Berzgale, the first NATO interception of a drone over Latvia.

incidents.label: Leipzig/Halle Airport
incidents.description: An FPV drone carrying 800 g of PETN struck the wing of an Antonov An-124 near its fuel tank and failed to detonate. A second drone hit a cargo jet on approach the next morning. The airport closed and the German federal prosecutor opened a case for attempted causing of an explosion.

incidents.label: Trans-Balkan pipeline, Kardam
incidents.site: Kardam, near the Trans-Balkan gas compressor station
incidents.description: A drone crossed undetected from Romania and exploded about a kilometre from the Trans-Balkan pipeline compressor station. Neither country's air defences saw it. Bulgaria's defence ministry assessed it as a Maya decoy drone of a type Ukraine uses, with no sign the target was deliberate.

incidents.label: Hannover Airport
incidents.description: Runways closed between 03:44 and 05:20 after airport staff and patrol officers repeatedly sighted a drone at roughly 25 m altitude. The airport's drone-detection system registered no signal at all. An internal police report said hybrid activity could not be ruled out.

incidents.label: NATO Eurofighter shootdown, Latvia
incidents.description: An Italian Eurofighter on Baltic Air Policing shot down a drone over Rugaji. It was later identified as Ukrainian, pushed off course by Russian electronic warfare.

incidents.label: NATO F-18 shootdown, Romania
incidents.description: A Spanish F-18 flying Romanian air policing shot down a drone that entered from the Moldovan side. Clearance ran through NATO's Combined Air Operations Centre rather than the national capital.

incidents.label: Neptun Deep gas field
incidents.site: Neptun Deep, Black Sea, about 80 nm east of Constanta
incidents.description: Romanian F-16s destroyed an explosive-laden sea drone with cannon fire at the Neptun Deep gas field, after NATO transferred engagement authority to Romanian forces.

incidents.label: Five drones over Stefan Voda district
incidents.site: Palanca and neighbouring villages, Stefan Voda district, on the Ukrainian border
incidents.description: Five drones crossed Moldova's southeastern frontier between 03:56 and 06:02 on Independence Day, one flying inland through Palanca, Crocmaz, Olanesti, Purcari and Rascaeti. Moldova's National Army Air Operations Service confirmed the flights and lost two drones from tracking. The parade in Chisinau went ahead.

incidents.label: Drone crossed into southeastern Estonia
incidents.site: Southeastern Estonia, Voru County border with Russia. Exact crossing point not released; marker at county level.
incidents.description: About a dozen drones were tracked along Estonia's eastern border during Ukrainian strikes on western Russia. One crossed into southeastern Estonia and another turned away short of Narva, said Air Force Commander Brigadier General Riivo Valge. Turkish F-16s scrambled from Amari and eight counties received an EE-ALARM shelter warning between 03:11 and 05:30. No drone fell and no aircraft fired.

incidents.label: Explosive drone found near Viisoara
incidents.site: Field outside Viisoara, Vaslui County, about 30 km from the Moldovan border
incidents.description: A damaged drone was found in a field outside Viisoara during a large Russian air attack on Ukraine. Romanian Intelligence Service specialists found it carried explosives and destroyed it in a controlled detonation. No casualties or damage.
